definitions.explanation: The time that will come after the present.
In grammar, the tense indicating future actions.

examples.japanese: {未来|みらい}のことは{誰|だれ}にも{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: No one knows what the future holds.

examples.japanese: {明|あか}るい{未来|みらい}を{夢見|ゆめみ}ている。
examples.english: I'm dreaming of a bright future.

examples.japanese: {未来|みらい}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: I'm looking forward to future technology.

notes:
RELATED TIME WORDS:
・{過去|かこ} (past)
・{現在|げんざい} (present)
・{未来|みらい} (future)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{未来|みらい}に{向|む}かって (toward the future)
・{未来|みらい}を{予測|よそく}する (to predict the future)
・{未来|みらい}を{描|えが}く (to envision the future)
・{明|あか}るい{未来|みらい} (bright future)
・{未来|みらい}{永劫|えいごう} (for all eternity)

GRAMMAR:
{未来|みらい}{形|けい} = future tense (grammatical term)

NOTE:
{未|み} means "not yet" and {来|らい} means "to come," so {未来|みらい} literally means "what has not yet come."
